per_metabolite.representation_rule: Write an aromatic or aliphatic nitro group in the PENTAVALENT form N(=O)=O, never in the charge-separated form [N+](=O)[O-]. eQuilibrator's group definition for the nitro group is the SMARTS '[C,c,N,n]N(=O)=O' (equilibrator_group_definitions.csv line 46, group name '-NO2'), which matches only the pentavalent spelling. The two spellings are the SAME molecule (identical RDKit canonical SMILES and identical InChIKey), so this is a representation rewrite, not a structure change. Two mechanical consequences: (1) the literal string must reach equilibrator_assets.molecule.Molecule.FromSmiles (OpenBabel) unmodified, because passing it through RDKit MolToSmiles rewrites it back to the charge-separated form and the decomposition then fails again; (2) LocalCompoundCache.get_compounds() resolves by InChIKey and returns the EXISTING cache row with its stored empty group vector, so handing it the fixed SMILES changes nothing; the group vector computed from the fixed SMILES must be written onto the compound object (or a cache row created that does not already exist). Reusable for any nitro species, including the ethylnitronate row.

NO working representation found. The pentavalent-nitro rewrite fixes the nitro half but a SECOND, independent gap remains: the group decomposer has no group for an ARYL phosphate ester. On 'O=N(=O)c1ccc(OP(=O)([O-])[O-])cc1' the phosphorus and its three oxygens (atom indices 8, 9, 10, 11) are left unassigned and the decomposition is refused. The same refusal occurs for plain phenyl phosphate 'c1ccccc1OP(=O)([O-])[O-]' with the nitro group absent, while ALIPHATIC phosphate esters (methyl phosphate, sn-glycerol 3-phosphate) decompose cleanly into the '-OPO3 [H0 Z-2 Mg0]' group. So the blocker is the aromatic-carbon-O-PO3 linkage, not the nitro function, and no SMILES rewrite of this molecule resolves it.

notes:
WHAT WAS FOUND, in three parts.

1. STRUCTURE, s_3860 (4-nitrophenol / 4-nitrophenolate). SOLVED, and the fix generalizes. eQuilibrator's nitro group definition is the SMARTS '[C,c,N,n]N(=O)=O', so the group decomposer matches only the PENTAVALENT spelling. This is the OPPOSITE of the hypothesis in the curation brief: the charge-separated [N+](=O)[O-] is what FAILS. The nitrobenzene control settles it, decomposing as 'O=N(=O)c1ccccc1' and failing as '[O-][N+](=O)c1ccccc1'. Both the phenolate '[O-]c1ccc(cc1)N(=O)=O' (formula C6H4NO3-, charge -1, exactly the GEM's) and the neutral phenol 'Oc1ccc(cc1)N(=O)=O' decompose. The phenolate group vector is '-NO2 [H0 Z0 Mg0] x 1 | ring >c-O [H0 Z-1 Mg0] x 1 | ring =c- [H1 Z0 Mg0] x 4 | ring =c< [H0 Z0 Mg0] x 1 | Origin x 1'. Injecting the neutral form's group vector in memory and calling ComponentContribution.standard_dg_formation returns a real number, standard dgf = -99.71 kJ/mol, and after Compound.transform at pH 7.2, I = 0.25 M, T = 303.15 K, pMg = 3.0, dgf' = +109.39 kJ/mol; this is a COMPUTED component-contribution estimate that follows once the structure is admitted, not a curated value, and it is quoted only to show the decomposition is productive rather than empty.

WHY THE CACHE IS STUCK, which the integrating code must handle. eQuilibrator's own compound cache already holds both molecules, s_3860 as compound 500 (reached by kegg:C00870, chebi:CHEBI:57917, metanetx.chemical:MNXM526) and s_3859 as compound 3341 (kegg:C03360, chebi:CHEBI:61146, metanetx.chemical:MNXM3867, bigg.metabolite:HC01104). Both store the CHARGE-SEPARATED SMILES and both store an EMPTY group vector, which is why standard_dg_formation returns None for each. Note the GEM's KEGG ids are C03360 and C00870, not the C08297 and C06214 guessed in the brief. LocalCompoundCache.get_compounds() resolves a submitted SMILES by InChIKey and hands back that same stale row, so simply feeding it the corrected string is a no-op, verified. The fix is to decompose the corrected SMILES directly with equilibrator_assets.group_decompose.GroupDecomposer and write the resulting vector onto the compound. Also verified: RDKit's MolToSmiles rewrites N(=O)=O back to [N+](=O)[O-], so any pipeline stage that canonicalizes through RDKit will silently undo the fix.

2. STRUCTURE, s_3859 (4-nitrophenyl phosphate). NOT SOLVED, and it is a different gap. With the nitro group written correctly the decomposition still fails, and the unassigned-atom dump names the phosphorus and its three oxygens. Plain phenyl phosphate with no nitro group fails identically, while methyl phosphate and sn-glycerol 3-phosphate decompose into '-OPO3 [H0 Z-2 Mg0]'. So the phosphate-chain finder does not recognize a phosphate hung off an AROMATIC ring oxygen. Mono-anion, di-anion and fully protonated forms all fail. This cannot be fixed by curating a structure; it needs a group definition or a measured value.

CONSEQUENCE FOR r_4220. The reaction needs both metabolites, so the s_3860 fix alone does NOT unblock r_4220. It does remove s_3860 from the blocking set, and it should be applied because it is reusable.

AN OPTION THAT WAS TRIED AND IS NOT ADMITTED. A group vector for the aryl phosphate can be assembled by hand as nitrobenzene with one 'ring =c- [H1]' promoted to 'ring =c< [H0]' plus one '-OPO3 [H0 Z-2]'. With that injected, ComponentContribution returns standard_dg = -57.9 +/- 2.8 and standard_dg_prime = -62.2 +/- 2.8 kJ/mol for r_4220 at pH 7.2, I = 0.25 M, T = 303.15 K, pMg = 3.0. The machinery is sound, since the same call on the fully decomposable sn-glycerol 3-phosphate hydrolysis control returns -13.0 +/- 2.1 kJ/mol, which is the right size for a phosphomonoester. But -62 kJ/mol is far more negative than a phosphomonoester hydrolysis should be, the hand-built vector has no fitted support for an -OPO3 group on an aromatic carbon, and nothing corroborates the magnitude. This is COMPUTED and it is NOT admitted. It is recorded so nobody repeats it and mistakes it for a result.

3. LITERATURE. The Goldberg 2009 primary is paywalled (Elsevier 403, Semantic Scholar reports openAccessPdf CLOSED), but its 4-nitrophenyl phosphate numbers were recovered VERBATIM from a NIST-deposited author manuscript by the same group on the nitrophenyl ACETATE reactions, which quotes [09GOL/LAN] on its working-notes pages. Recovered, all at the standard state of the hypothetical ideal solution of unit molality:
  chemical reference reaction, 4-nitrophenyl phosphate(2-)(aq) + H2O(l) = 4-nitrophenol(aq) + HPO4(2-)(aq), drH0 = -(13.7 +/- 0.5) kJ/mol;
  ionization, 4-nitrophenyl phosphate(-) = H+ + 4-nitrophenyl phosphate(2-), pK = 5.42, drH0 = -9.2 kJ/mol;
  ionization, H2PO4(-) = H+ + HPO4(2-), pK = 7.198, drH0 = 3.6 kJ/mol;
  ionization, 4-nitrophenol(0) = H+ + 4-nitrophenol(-), pK = 7.15, drH0 = 19.4 kJ/mol (uncertain by +/- 0.01 and +/- 2), from Marcus and Smith [03MAR/SMI] via the same artifact;
  derived by the authors, 4-nitrophenyl phosphate(-) + H2O(l) = 4-nitrophenol(aq) + H2PO4(-), drH0 = -26.5 kJ/mol.
The temperature is not stated in the quoted lines; Goldberg's standard is T = 298.15 K and that is the reading I would apply, but it is UNVERIFIED from this artifact.

THIS IS AN ENTHALPY AND ONLY AN ENTHALPY. The archived abstract of the 2009 paper says in so many words that the apparent equilibrium constant was measured for reaction (2), sn-glycerol 3-phosphate, not for reaction (3), ours. A calorimetric drH0 fixes the temperature dependence of the equilibrium, not its position; it cannot be turned into a drG without a second measurement or an entropy. So it is admissible as an ENTHALPY, and it must NOT be entered as a Gibbs energy for r_4220. That is why this record's kind is 'structure' and not 'reaction_energy': there is no drG to record.

TABULATED FORMATION DATA for 4-nitrophenol, for completeness. NIST WebBook gives only gas and solid enthalpies of formation (solid -212.4 +/- 1.0 kJ/mol Finch 1983, -207.1 +/- 1.1 Sabbah 1994; gas -117.7 +/- 2.0 and -114.7 +/- 1.2) and NO Gibbs energy of formation and NO aqueous data. The Goldberg-group manuscript carries these through a solution enthalpy to drfH0 = -190.53 kJ/mol for 4-nitrophenol(aq), again an enthalpy. Converting any of this to an aqueous drfG would require a solvation model, which would make it 'computed' and inadmissible.

WHAT A HUMAN STILL NEEDS TO DO.
  a. Get the Goldberg 2009 primary through the university subscription (doi:10.1016/j.jct.2008.12.017) and confirm the temperature and ionic strength attached to drH0 = -(13.7 +/- 0.5), and check whether its Table of chemical reference reactions reports a K for reaction (3) obtained from the literature rather than measured. The archived abstract says the equilibrium model 'was then used to calculate thermodynamic property values (equilibrium constants K and standard enthalpies of reaction) for chemical reference reactions', which leaves open that a K for reaction (3) appears in the paper sourced from elsewhere. That is the single highest-value unresolved question in this row.
  b. Chase Axelrod, 'The Free Energy of Hydrolysis of p-Nitrophenyl Phosphate', Science 114 (1951) 525-526, doi:10.1126/science.114.2968.525. It is the only drG lead found for this exact reaction and it is behind an AAAS 403. If it reports a measured free energy of hydrolysis, that value, not the enthalpy, is what closes r_4220.
  c. Sturtevant, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 77 (1955) 255-258, is an independent calorimetric drH for the same reaction and would corroborate the -13.7.
  d. Decide whether to add a group definition for an aryl phosphate ester to eQuilibrator's group set. That is a change to the shared group table with consequences for every aromatic phosphate in the GEM, so it is a decision, not a fix, and it needs the author.
  e. The TECRDB search interface at randr.nist.gov/enzyme is dead, so if a TECRDB entry for EC 3.1.3.1 or 3.1.3.2 with 4-nitrophenyl phosphate matters, it has to come from the printed compilations (Goldberg and Tewari, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data) rather than the web database.
